# dtcloud_security_group (Data Source)

Looks up one security group, by id or by name.

Use it to reference a group Terraform did not create. The name lookup spares a hand-copied id:
`security_groups` on a machine's network interface takes ids.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# By id.
data "dtcloud_security_group" "web" {
  id = var.security_group_id
}

# Or by name -- the lookup fails rather than guessing if the name matches more
# than one group.
data "dtcloud_security_group" "app" {
  name = "app-tier"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `id` (String) ID of the security group to look up. Give this or `name`.
- `name` (String) Name of the security group to look up. Give this or `id`. Must match exactly one group.

### Read-Only

- `description` (String) Description of the security group.
- `inbound_rule` (List of Object) Inbound rules as the platform displays them. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--inbound_rule))
- `outbound_rule` (List of Object) Outbound rules as the platform displays them. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--outbound_rule))

<a id="nestedatt--inbound_rule"></a>
### Nested Schema for `inbound_rule`

Read-Only:

- `id` (String)
- `port_range` (String)
- `protocol` (String)
- `source` (String)


<a id="nestedatt--outbound_rule"></a>
### Nested Schema for `outbound_rule`

Read-Only:

- `id` (String)
- `port_range` (String)
- `protocol` (String)
- `source` (String)

## Behaviour worth knowing

* **A name must match exactly one group.** Names are not unique on the platform, so a name that
  matches several groups is an error rather than an arbitrary pick. Look the group up by id instead.
* **The rule blocks are a display**, as on the resource: `protocol` is a display name, `port_range` is
  text, and `source` is a CIDR or another group's name. Their `id` is the second half of a
  `dtcloud_security_group_rule` import id.
